4-Week Contract Role | Townsville   Your new company     This established Townsville-based organisation is undertaking a significant data quality and system improvement project to enhance the accuracy and consistency of its product catalogue and ERP system. With a strong focus on operational excellence and process improvement, the business is seeking a detail-oriented administrator to support this important initiative.    Your new role     As a Product Data Auditor, you will play a key role in reviewing, correcting, and standardising approximately 8,000 part records within a leading ERP system. This is a detail-focused role requiring accuracy, consistency, and the ability to maintain high-quality product data while following established standards and processes.     Your responsibilities will include:    
 
 Reviewing part records against an audit spreadsheet and established data standards   
 Updating and standardising product descriptions and naming conventions   
 Verifying and correcting part numbers   
 Reviewing and updating product images   
 Maintaining and enhancing product search terms   
 Checking pricing structures and identifying discrepancies   
 Confirming products are assigned to the correct catalogue groups   
 Recording audit outcomes, comments, and follow-up actions   
 Updating and maintaining accurate data within ERP systems and Excel   
 Escalating uncertain or incomplete information for review     
 
  What you'll need to succeed     
 
 Previous experience in data entry, data cleansing, data auditing, or catalogue administration 
 Exceptional attention to detail and a high level of accuracy 
 Strong Microsoft Excel skills, including filtering, sorting, and working with large datasets 
 Confidence working within ERP, database, or business management systems 
 Excellent written English and the ability to follow strict formatting standards 
 Strong organisational and time management skills 
 The ability to work independently and maintain consistent quality 
 
  Desirable:  
 
 Experience using simPRO or similar ERP software 
 Experience maintaining product catalogues or inventory data 
 Exposure to mechanical, engineering, industrial, hydraulic, or fastener terminology 
 
   What you'll get in return     
 
 A 4-week temporary assignment with the possibility of permanency for the right candidate   
 Full training and onboarding provided   
 Exposure to a leading ERP system and business processes   
 A structured project with clear objectives and procedures   
 Monday to Friday office-based hours in Townsville   
 The opportunity to contribute to a significant business improvement initiative   
 A supportive and collaborative team environment   
 
      What you need to do now     If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV to Georgia.Mathews@hays.com.au, or call us now on  +61 7 4417 1135.   If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion about your career.    Please  click here  to apply.

result.description:
Perfection Fresh Australia Pty Ltd is a leading Australian fresh produce company specialising in the growing, sourcing, marketing, and distribution of premium-quality fruit and vegetables. The company is committed to sustainable horticultural practices, ethical sourcing, and innovation, working closely with growers and industry partners to deliver high-quality produce while promoting a culture of excellence, collaboration, and safety. We are seeking a full time Research, Development & Analysis Manager to join our berry division. In this role, you will lead the design, coordination, and analysis of berry research, trial, and performance programs across Perfection Fresh Australia-owned farms and selected third-party growers. This role will be based in Caboolture, QLD.

Base salary: $79,423 per annum (plus super)

Main Responsibilities:
•	Determine, implement and monitor berry research and development strategies, trial programs and project plans aligned with commercial and production objectives.
•	Develop and coordinate research projects and variety trials across company farms and grower sites, including trial design, methodologies, timelines and data collection.
•	Lead and coordinate research activities by working with farm managers, growers, breeders, nursery partners and technical stakeholders to achieve project objectives.
•	Assess the effectiveness and commercial outcomes of research and development activities by evaluating varietal performance, yield, quality, harvest efficiency, labour productivity and grower returns.
•	Collect, analyse and interpret research and production data to identify trends, evaluate trial outcomes and support evidence-based decision-making.
•	Evaluate new berry varieties and production practices and recommend commercialisation strategies and operational improvements based on research findings.
•	Provide technical advice and research-based recommendations to management, production teams and growers on varietal selection, production practices and continuous improvement initiatives.
•	Monitor emerging developments in berry production, breeding programs and research methodologies, and assess their potential application to the organisation's research priorities.
•	Prepare and maintain research reports, trial records, databases and technical documentation, and communicate research findings to internal and external stakeholders.

Required Qualification and Experience:
•	A bachelor's in a related field to horticultural/agricultural science.
•	At least 2 years of work experience in horticulture, agriculture, berry production, agronomy, research and development, trial coordination, data analysis or a closely related technical role.

Ideal Skills and Attributes:
•	Strong data collection, analysis and interpretation skills, with the ability to convert data into practical operational recommendations.

result.description:
SK tes is a global leader in sustainable technology lifecycle services, providing end-to-end IT asset management solutions spanning deployment, decommissioning, reuse and recycling. Operating 40+ owned facilities across more than 20 countries and supporting clients worldwide, SK tes processes and managing large-scale technology assets with a strong focus on security, compliance, and value recovery. Guided by its mission to “securely, safely, and sustainably transform and re-purpose one billion kilograms of assets by 2030,” the organisation leverages innovation and global capability to deliver meaningful outcomes for both clients and the environment.

About the Role

Company: SK tes Pty Ltd
Location: Union Cct YATALA QLD 4207
Job Type: Casual 
Salary/Rate: Award Rates Apply (Paid in accordance with the relevant Modern Award)

Role Overview

An IT Recycle Operator is responsible for the proper disposal and recycling of information technology (IT) equipment that has reached the end of its useful life. The role involves handling electronic waste (e-waste) in an environmentally responsible manner, ensuring compliance with regulations, and promoting sustainable practices. The IT Recycle Operator plays a crucial role in reducing the environmental impact of discarded IT assets and supporting the organization's commitment to responsible recycling. 

An operator will work across a multitude of departments in our production facilities. Operators will be efficient and reliable in processing, organising and packing of assets. 

Where an operator has the necessary licences, training and ability, an operator may be required to operate machinery as directed by their line manager.

Key Accountabilities

•	Be responsible for the quality assurance of their own work.
•	Works under routine supervision, either individually or in a team environment.
•	Being able to lift to 15kg.
•	Complete necessary training materials, a directed by the business.
•	Follow all reasonable directions of the Team Leader.
•	Maintain accurate records and inventory of all disposed assets.
•	Some of the daily work activities include receiving, sorting, testing, warehousing, data destruction, and de-manufacturing.
•	General tasks associated with the receiving and dispatch of assets.
•	Able to maintain records or reports in accordance with company procedures.
•	Operators will rotate and work across a multitude of departments in our production facilities and be efficient and reliable in processing, organising and packing of assets.
•	Perform data sanitization and secure data destruction processes on all retired IT assets to prevent data breaches and ensure compliance with data protection regulations.
•	Safely and responsibly handle the dismantling and disposal of electronic components following proper procedures.
•	Conduct accurate testing and assessment of returned assets to determine their potential for refurbishment or reuse as per the guidelines.
•	Conduct Inventory Stock Take activities.
•	May be directed to perform other duties consistent with training and skill levels required for this position.
•	Maintaining confidentiality and ensuring data security throughout the ITAD process.

Job Requirements & Qualifications

•	Experience in Warehousing (Preferable) 
•	A valid forklift licence is a PLUS but not required
•	Effective communication skills
•	Basic admin/data entry capability
•	Understanding of IT hardware components and familiarity with various types of electronic devices.
•	Physical fitness to handle and move electronic equipment.
•	Ability to operate recycling machinery and equipment safely and efficiently.
•	Strong attention to detail to ensure proper sorting and disposal of e-waste.

What We Offer

•	Competitive remuneration package
•	Career progression opportunities
•	Ongoing training and professional development
•	Supportive and collaborative team environment
•	Opportunity to be part of a growing global organisation focused on sustainability and innovation

About CALHN
At Central Adelaide (CALHN), we're shaping the future of health through excellence in clinical care, research, and innovation. As South Australia's largest health network, we deliver exceptional, safe and connected healthcare - for our patients, our community, and our people.

With more than 17,000 dedicated employees, every day at CALHN presents an opportunity to make a real impact-not because it's expected, but because our values guide us to be our best. Find out more about CALHN sites and services, our stories and the opportunities to be part of CALHN.

About the Role

The role is to Coordinate and undertake the collection, validation, entry, submission and reporting of cardiothoracic surgical data for the Royal Adelaide Hospital to national clinical registries including ANZSCTS and ANZTHOR. The role contributes to clinical governance, quality improvement, benchmarking, research and service planning by ensuring the provision of accurate, timely and complete data in accordance with legislative, ethical and organisational requirements.Ideally, an ANZSCTS Data Manager would possess the following skills and experience:

Cardiac nursing or ICU nursing experience (or equivalent)

Competency with Microsoft Office software (Word, Excel)

Proficiency in the use of web browsers

Strong communication and interpersonal skills

Excellent organisation and time management skills

Proven experience with data entry and attention to detail

About You

You're an organised and detail focused professional who enjoys turning clinical data into meaningful insights while supporting quality patient care.

- Experience in clinical data or health registries
- Skilled in data analysis with strong attention to detail
- Manage priorities and work with initiative
- Build strong relationships across healthcare teams
- Understand data privacy, governance and quality standards

Why You'll Love It Here - CALHN benefits that matter
We know that a great career is about more than just the work you do, it's also about the support you receive. At CALHN, you'll enjoy :

Salary packaging - up to $9,010 for living expenses + $2,650 for meals & entertainment + pre-tax super & novated lease options

Safe connections - be part of a culture of safety and connectivity, focusing on outcomes and continuous improvements

Recognition & growth - celebrate success and explore opportunities across CALHN's many sites

Flexible work options - speak to us about flexibility options for this role to suit your lifestyle

Paid leave - with leave loading for rest and recharge

Health & fitness perks - discounted access to Fitness Passport & free flu vaccinations

Wellbeing support - Employee Assistance Program for you & your family

Diversity & Inclusion
We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and supported. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disabilities, culturally diverse backgrounds, and LGBTQIA+ communities.

result.description:
For nearly 25 years, APD Global has set the benchmark in delivering advanced, comprehensive, and specialised engineering solutions.

We have around 800 employees including our alliance contracting partners, across 15 strategically located offices in Australia (Perth, Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Adelaide, Darwin), New Zealand and Malaysia. We specialise in seamless integration across the Power Systems, Telecommunications, and Renewable Energy industries. Our expertise spans Power Systems Studies, Transmission Lines, Substations, Telecommunications, Protection, Control & Automation, Renewable Energy Connections, Mining, and Engineering, Protection Panel Design and Installation, 3D Design and Manufacturing as well as Construction/Management (EPC/M) services.

We have outstanding opportunity for a highly experienced and skilled ENGINEERING TECHNOLOGIST to join our team across all states in Australia. We are looking for trustworthy individuals with integrity who will bring a positive can-do attitude to the position and to the team. Position available in Vic, Qld, WA, 
and NSW.

The Role
A space-based Engineering Technologist at a power company primarily uses satellite technology to enhance the power grid. This role requires the successful candidate to manage projects from start to finish, ensuring the effective and cohesive operation of both space and ground systems to meet the company's operational and strategic goals.

Key duties involve: Designing and implementing satellite communication systems, Utilising satellite data for grid analysis, and Integrating space-based technology into existing ground infrastructure.

Core duties
System design and architecture: Design and define the architecture for satellite-based communication, monitoring, or sensing systems to be used by the power company. This includes analyzing performance and technical specifications.
Power and communication integration: Ensure that satellite power systems and communication links are compatible with the power company's ground infrastructure and can transmit data and commands reliably.
Mission and project management: Oversee the entire lifecycle of a project, including research, design, development, testing, and deployment of space-based assets, ensuring they meet the company's objectives.
Stakeholder management: Coordinate with internal teams (e.g., grid operations, IT, finance) and external partners (e.g., satellite operators, vendors) to ensure seamless integration and collaboration.
Data analysis: Work with and analyze data from satellites to support power grid management, such as monitoring assets, predicting demand, or assessing grid health and stability.
Technical oversight: Ensure that all subsystems of a space-based system function correctly together, addressing any integration issues or performance bottlenecks that arise.
Testing and validation: Develop and execute test plans for new systems and validate that they meet performance and safety requirements before and during deployment.
Risk and compliance management: Identify and manage risks associated with using space-based technology and ensure compliance with relevant regulations and standards.

Example scenario:
A power company might employ a space-based systems engineer to create a system for real-time monitoring of remote substations. The engineer would design a system using a constellation of small satellites to collect data.

Their duties would include:
Defining the requirements for the satellite communication system, including data rates and latency.
Designing the satellite payload and its integration with the company's ground control software.
Ensuring the system's power budget is adequate for its mission lifespan.
Testing the system on the ground to verify its performance before launch.
Collaborating with the satellite operator to ensure smooth data delivery once the system is operational

If you have the skills required for this role and you feel this is the job for you, then apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super
